column1: # scripts/guard-registry.tsv: one row for every hook a shipped template runs or install.sh writes, and every `scripts/ci-gates.sh` gate (#1592). A script no template wires (a CI-only gate script, a hand-installed hook) has no row; `ci-gates.sh rails` covers its `# rail:` header.
# `ci-gates.sh guard-registry --registry scripts/guard-registry.tsv .` fails on a guard with no row, a row with an empty owner, reason or date,
# and a row for a guard that no longer exists: add the row when you add the guard, delete it when you remove the guard.
# FORMAT: `<id><TAB><owner role><TAB><reason><TAB><review-by YYYY-MM-DD>[<TAB><fire log>]`. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.
#   id: `hook:<skill>/<script>` (a script a shipped templates/*.settings.json runs), `hook:.githooks/<name>` (a git hook install.sh writes) or `gate:<name>` (a ci-gates.sh subcommand).
#   owner role: a lowercase slug naming a skill or role, never a person. reason: one clause on what the guard stops. review-by: the day the owner next confirms it still earns its friction.

#   fire log: optional path (`~` and $VARs expanded) of a log holding one `YYYY-MM-DD ...` line per fire; without one, or when the log is missing, emptied or holds no dated line, the report says "unknown", never "zero fires". The reply_cap row names the default location only: REPLY_CAP_LOG or XDG_CACHE_HOME moves the real log, and the report then reads the wrong file.
# `ci-gates.sh guard-registry --report [--days N] --registry scripts/guard-registry.tsv .` lists the rows past review-by and the logged guards with no fire in N days (default 30).
# It is read-only: it never edits or deletes a row. To confirm a guard, bump its review-by; to retire one, remove the guard and its row together.
# The `hook:<skill>/<script>` rows repeat the owner, reason and review date of the script's own `# rail:` header (scripts/test-guard-registry.sh keeps the two equal).

column3: rerun the fast lint and unit tier before every push (opt in with core.hooksPath)
deny a git hook bypass: fix the failing hook instead
keep the main session delegating instead of hand-editing source
warn when a PR or tracker write misses its artifact template
nudge a handoff at a huge context since long sessions re-read it every turn
ask the owner only after a recorded evil-twin and council pass
deny destructive host commands before they run (best effort; the OS sandbox is the boundary)
deny gh issue create when the same finding is already filed
stop starting PRs while ready ones wait unmerged; alarm on a stalled flow
deny git push and gh pr merge while a freeze is on
cap a subagent handback and audit each lane's prose
re-inject a short handoff after a compact so the plan survives
defer a heavy local command while the machine is busy
flag a merge pipeline that landed nothing while green PRs wait
tell a lane to checkpoint near its tool-call cap
advise resuming an earlier same-domain lane over a costly new one
no fixed/faster/done claim on a delivery outcome without a measurement
keep an installed Perun current with no manual step
flag a gate or push piped to tail/head/grep that masks its exit status
deny a GitHub write whose title or body matches the repo banlist except into a sibling repo of the origin owner and deny a write into Perun that names the session repository
nudge when the same command runs more than 3 times in a session
owner rule: chat replies max 3 lines and 500 chars
surface at most 3 lines of fleet hygiene at session start
nudge when an autonomous turn ends stopped or waiting with work still open
stop a subagent brief that names a tool the lane does not have
inject the house standing defaults into every new subagent
opt-in reply budget stated up front (never forces a rewrite)
no banned name, identifier or secret pattern in a file the repo ships
every references file is routed from its SKILL.md and no SKILL.md outgrows the byte cap
VERSION is exact core semver and the first changelog heading announces it
the real installer lands each mode and the vendored docs are real, not placeholders
every shipped skill appears in all five hand-maintained lists
every shipped SKILL.md and reference stays within its frozen byte budget
a size budget rises only with a size-budget-raise marker
a changelog fragment carries the exact size-budget-raise marker and no release heading
no tracked image, media, archive or build-output file
the always-paid MUST-LOAD cost per archetype stays within its frozen ceiling
a MUST, NEVER or ALWAYS rule names a mechanism or says advisory, and the unenforced baseline only shrinks
every test script is run by CI or listed with a reason
every guard and hook script carries its owner, reason and review date in its header
every installed hook and every gate has one row with an owner role, a reason and a review-by date
